proposal.hypothesis: The selected parent uses up to 16,384 partials and measured 0.000473368 s; a correct 4,096-partial candidate measured 0.000289782 s. This tests an intermediate cap of 6,144 with the same 4,096-element target: at the largest input it reduces first-stage CTA count and finalizer fan-in versus the parent while retaining more parallelism than the 4,096-cap candidate. The tradeoff may balance first-stage work and finalization, but no speedup is assumed.

retained: Retain the fused first-stage sum(abs(x)) with contiguous scalar loads and a 256-thread CUB block reduction.
Keep ceil(n/4096) partials until the cap, reducing the maximum from 16,384 to 6,144; proportionally partition the input using ceil(n/partial_count).
Retain one final CTA to reduce all current-call partials and overwrite output; preserve explicit zero output for non-positive n.
